rationale: In Genesis 18:26-32 the LORD agrees that a number of righteous people would spare a whole city ('On account of the ten, I will not destroy it,' 18:32, BSB). Ezekiel 14:12-20 states the reverse outcome four times, for a land that 'sins against Me by acting unfaithfully': 'even if these three men—Noah, Daniel, and Job—were in it, their righteousness could deliver only themselves' (14:14). Keil and Delitzsch, on Ezekiel 14:14, read the passage as answering a hope drawn from Genesis 18: the earlier threat 'left the possibility still open, that He would avert the destruction of Judah and Jerusalem for the sake of the righteous therein, as He had promised the patriarch Abraham that He would do in the case of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 18:23.). This hope ... is now to be taken from the people.' Calvin, on Genesis 18:23, makes a related contrast from the other side without naming Ezekiel: 'He who would have spared Sodom on account of ten righteous persons, refused to grant the same terms of pardon to Jerusalem.' Graded contrast_reversal because Ezekiel states the opposite result for the case it describes: the righteous deliver only themselves rather than sparing the place. Graded plausible because only Keil and Delitzsch, of the commentaries read on Ezekiel 14:14, draws the Genesis 18 link; several of the others cross-reference Jeremiah 15:1 instead. Ezekiel names neither Abraham nor Sodom, and the key verbs differ ('deliver' in Ezekiel is natsal, not Genesis 18's nasa, 'spare'). Whether the two passages conflict or describe different situations is left open in the lesson.
